question: Which of the following plateaus, with an average elevation of 500 m, is spread over Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Malwa Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Malwa Plateau is located in the central-western part of India, primarily spread over the states of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.
 
• It has an average elevation of around 500 meters above sea level, making it a significant geographic feature in the region.
 
• The plateau is known for its rich black soil, which is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture, especially the cultivation of crops like cotton and soybeans.
 
• The region is also known for its historical significance and houses several important archaeological sites and cultural heritage landmarks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marwar Plateau**

 
 
• Also known as the Marusthali region, it is located in the western part of Rajasthan.
 
• It is characterized by sandy and rocky terrain with an arid climate.
 
• The plateau is part of the Thar Desert and is not as elevated as the Malwa Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau**
 
 
• This plateau covers a large part of southern India, extending across multiple states like Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It has an average elevation of about 600 meters above sea level and is known for its volcanic basalt rock formations.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is different from the Malwa Plateau in terms of geological formation and climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Chota Nagpur Plateau**
 
 
• Located in eastern India, it spans across the states of Jharkhand, West Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
 
• It is rich in mineral resources like coal, iron ore, and bauxite.
 
• The Chota Nagpur Plateau has a rugged terrain with an average elevation of around 700 meters.
